input.strategy_title: Bring-your-own vector database for RAG workloads
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RAG applications built on Llama Stack need a vector store, and today the
platform neither ships one nor documents how to attach an external one.
Customers are split into two camps with incompatible expectations: regulated
customers want a platform-managed vector database with supported images and
lifecycle, while cloud-native customers already run managed services (e.g.
a cloud vector DB) and only want a sanctioned way to connect them. We have not
decided which posture to productize first, and the answer changes most of the
downstream work.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the first supported vector store posture: platform-managed (operator-deployed Milvus) versus external-connection-only. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Depending on that decision: either administrators can deploy the managed vector store through the Platform Operator with productized images, or data scientists can register an external vector store connection per project with validated connectivity. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | The Dashboard exposes the chosen integration (deploy-and-manage UI for the managed path, or connection management UI for the external path). |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Product documentation covers setup and limits for whichever posture ships. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- Shipping both postures in the same release
- Embedding model selection and lifecycle (separate strategy)

## Open Questions

1. Managed Milvus versus external-connection-only is genuinely undecided — the
   evaluation in HLR-1 must weigh supportability cost, disconnected-environment
   viability, and time-to-market, and the outcome forks the implementation
   structure for HLR-2 through HLR-5.

# Midstream repo onboarding for Milvus under opendatahub-io

## Description

This epic creates the midstream Milvus repository under opendatahub-io so the
platform can build productized Milvus images for the managed vector store
posture. Milvus is not currently in the platform inventory; this is the first
step of the onboarding chain for the managed path.

## Scope

- Create the opendatahub-io midstream fork of the upstream Milvus project,
  tracking the upstream release chosen for productization.
- Apply the midstream conventions used by other opendatahub-io repositories
  (branching, upstream sync process, repository metadata).
- Establish the commit/branch baseline from which the productized container
  image build will run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The upstream Milvus release to be productized is explicitly selected in this
  epic: the exact release version and the selection rationale (support window,
  known-issue fit for the managed posture) are recorded in the repository
  metadata, so downstream license scanning and image builds consume a pinned,
  documented choice.
- A midstream Milvus repository exists under opendatahub-io, tracking the
  selected upstream Milvus release.
- The repository's branching and sync conventions match those of other
  opendatahub-io midstream repositories.
- The repository baseline is reproducible: the exact upstream version and any
  midstream patches applied are recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, managed path): administrators can deploy the managed vector
  store with productized images — this epic provides the repository those
  images are built from.

# License validation for Milvus and transitive dependencies

## Description

This epic runs license scanning over Milvus and its transitive dependencies to
confirm the managed posture is shippable with productized images. It runs in
parallel with the midstream repository onboarding and gates the general
managed-deployment implementation: if licenses fail, the dependency set
changes and the approach is affected.

## Scope

- Run license scanning over the selected upstream Milvus release and its
  transitive dependencies, using the platform's standard license-validation
  tooling and recipe.
- Produce a scan report covering all dependencies pulled into the productized
  image.
- Record a disposition for every finding (acceptable, or remediation needed),
  escalated to the owning team where a license conflict is found.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A license scan report exists covering Milvus and its full transitive
  dependency set for the selected release.
- Every license finding in the report has a recorded disposition.
- Any blocking license conflict is raised with a documented remediation path
  before the managed-deployment implementation proceeds.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, managed path): productized images for the managed vector store
  require a license-clean dependency set.

# Konflux onboarding for the productized Milvus image build

## Description

This epic onboards the midstream Milvus repository to Konflux so the
productized Milvus container image is built by the platform's standard build
and release pipeline. It starts once the midstream repository exists and runs
in parallel with the operator deployment implementation — the build pipeline
configuration does not depend on the operator code.

## Scope

- Add the Konflux build pipeline configuration for the productized Milvus
  image to the midstream Milvus repository, following the known Konflux
  onboarding recipe.
- Wire the image build application and release stream so the productized
  image is produced from the midstream repository baseline.
- Verify the pipeline produces a buildable image from the repository.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Konflux pipeline for the productized Milvus image runs to completion on
  the midstream repository.
- The pipeline produces a container image from the repository baseline
  without manual build steps.
- The onboarding follows the standard Konflux recipe with no repo-specific
  custom pipeline logic beyond documented exceptions.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, managed path): productized images for the managed vector store
  require a platform build pipeline.

# Platform Operator deployment and lifecycle for managed Milvus

## Description

This epic delivers the core of the managed posture: administrators can deploy
the platform-managed vector store (Milvus) through the Platform Operator,
using the productized image, with platform-supported lifecycle. It is the
general implementation of the onboarding chain — it runs after license
validation and in parallel with the Konflux build-pipeline onboarding.

## Scope

- Extend the Platform Operator so an administrator can deploy the managed
  Milvus vector store as a platform resource, referencing the productized
  Milvus image.
- Implement lifecycle handling for the managed vector store (deployment,
  status reporting, upgrade, and removal) at the level the platform provides
  for other operator-managed components.
- Surface deployment status through the operator's standard status
  conditions so consuming components and the Dashboard can observe it.
- Confirm the Platform Operator's ownership and extension surface with the
  owning team before starting — the Platform Operator has no
  architecture-context file in the platform inventory (see decomposition
  health warnings).

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can deploy the managed Milvus vector store through the
  Platform Operator, and the deployment reports ready status.
- The deployment uses the productized Milvus image (pinned digest available
  at deployment time) rather than an ad-hoc upstream image reference.
- Lifecycle operations (upgrade, removal) are available for the managed
  vector store and leave the cluster in a consistent state.
- The build pipeline for the changed operator code is green (the Konflux
  onboarding in this strategy's dependency chain gates first execution, not
  this epic's start).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, managed path): administrators can deploy the managed vector
  store through the Platform Operator with productized images.

# Llama Stack RAG provider integration for the managed vector store

## Description

This epic wires the managed vector store into Llama Stack as a RAG provider,
so Llama Stack distributions running on the platform can use the
operator-deployed Milvus without anyone hand-editing distribution
configuration files. Llama Stack exposes a provider-plugin model for RAG
providers, and its architecture context already lists Milvus/vector providers
as the expected backing for RAG workflows.

## Scope

- Integrate the managed vector store as the RAG (vector) provider for Llama
  Stack distributions on the platform, using the provider-plugin configuration
  model the Llama Stack distribution already supports.
- Make the provider configuration discoverable from the platform-side managed
  deployment (the operator-provisioned vector store instance) rather than
  requiring hand-edited distribution config files.
- Verify the integration end to end with a RAG workload that stores and
  retrieves embeddings through the managed vector store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack distribution can be configured to use the managed vector
  store as its RAG provider through supported configuration surfaces — no
  hand-editing of distribution config files.
- A RAG workload run against the distribution stores and retrieves embeddings
  through the managed vector store successfully.
- The integration works against the operator-deployed instance without
  hard-coded connection details in the distribution configuration.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector store
  as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs.

# Dashboard deploy-and-manage UI for the managed vector store

## Description

This epic exposes the managed vector store in the Dashboard: administrators
can deploy and manage the operator-managed Milvus instance from the platform
console. The Dashboard reads and writes the operator's custom resources and
owns no data plane, so this epic builds the console surface on top of the
operator-provided deployment capability.

## Scope

- Add a Dashboard surface where administrators can deploy the managed vector
  store and observe its status, backed by the operator's custom resources and
  status conditions.
- Provide management operations in the console consistent with the lifecycle
  the operator supports (deployment, status, upgrade, removal).
- Follow the Dashboard's existing per-component feature flag and defaults
  mechanism for enabling the managed vector store surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can deploy the managed vector store from the Dashboard and
  see its readiness status in the console.
- Management operations available in the console reflect the lifecycle
  supported by the operator, with no data-plane logic implemented in the
  Dashboard.
- The surface is gated by the Dashboard's standard feature flag mechanism.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1, managed path): the Dashboard exposes a deploy-and-manage UI for
  the managed vector store.

# Documentation for the platform-managed vector store posture

## Description

This epic authors the product documentation for the platform-managed vector
store posture: how administrators deploy and manage the operator-managed
Milvus vector store, and the setup steps and limits of the managed offering.
It runs last in the managed branch — the documentation describes what was
actually built.

## Scope

- Author the documentation topic covering setup and configuration of the
  managed vector store through the Platform Operator and the Dashboard.
- Document the supported limits of the managed posture (scale, connectivity,
  and any restrictions identified during implementation).
- Document how Llama Stack distributions consume the managed vector store as
  a RAG provider.
- Content outline: managed vector store setup (administrator workflow),
  lifecycle management, Dashboard usage, Llama Stack RAG provider
  consumption, limits and support boundaries.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Product documentation exists covering setup and limits for the
  platform-managed vector store posture.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  behavior of the managed deployment, Dashboard UI, and Llama Stack provider
  integration, and discrepancies found in review are fixed.
- The documentation covers both the administrator (deploy and manage) and
  data-scientist (RAG consumption) perspectives.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P2): product documentation covers setup and limits for whichever
  posture ships — this epic covers the managed posture.

# Llama Stack RAG provider integration for registered external vector stores

## Description

This epic wires registered external vector store connections into Llama
Stack as RAG providers, so Llama Stack distributions on the platform can use
a project's registered external vector store without anyone hand-editing
distribution configuration files. Llama Stack exposes a provider-plugin
model for RAG providers, and its architecture context lists Milvus/vector
providers as the expected backing for RAG workflows.

## Scope

- Integrate registered external vector store connections as the RAG
  (vector) provider source for Llama Stack distributions, using the
  provider-plugin configuration model the Llama Stack distribution already
  supports.
- Resolve provider configuration from the project's registered connections
  rather than requiring hand-edited distribution config files.
- Verify the integration end to end with a RAG workload that stores and
  retrieves embeddings through a registered external vector store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack distribution can be configured to use a project's registered
  external vector store connection as its RAG provider through supported
  configuration surfaces — no hand-editing of distribution config files.
- A RAG workload run against the distribution stores and retrieves embeddings
  through the registered external vector store successfully.
- Credentials from the registered connection are consumed through the
  platform's secret handling, not duplicated into distribution config files.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen vector store
  as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs — external
  path.

# Vector store posture decision: managed vs external-connection-only

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's gating unknown: which vector store
posture the platform productizes first for RAG workloads — a platform-managed
vector database (operator-deployed Milvus with productized images and
lifecycle) or an external-connection-only posture (data scientists register an
existing, customer-operated vector store per project). The strategy
deliberately leaves this undecided, and the outcome determines which
downstream implementation epics exist.

## Scope

- Produce a documented evaluation comparing the two postures against the
  criteria the strategy names: supportability cost, disconnected-environment
  viability, and time-to-market.
- Weigh the two customer camps described in the strategy: regulated customers
  who want a platform-managed vector database, and cloud-native customers who
  already run managed vector services and want a sanctioned way to connect
  them.
- Record a single posture decision with rationale, traceable to the
  evaluation, and identify which downstream implementation structure the
  decision selects (managed onboarding chain vs connection registration).
- Confirm feasibility inputs for the chosen posture only as needed to make the
  decision defensible (for example, whether a productized Milvus image is
  supportable in disconnected environments); this investigation does not
  implement either posture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written evaluation exists that compares platform-managed
  (operator-deployed Milvus) versus external-connection-only against
  supportability cost, disconnected-environment viability, and
  time-to-market, with the trade-offs for each criterion stated explicitly.
- A single posture decision is recorded with rationale that references the
  evaluation.
- The decision record states which downstream implementation structure
  applies, so implementation epics can be scheduled without re-litigating the
  decision.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): a decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the
  first supported vector store posture.
